claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than commercial pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than commercial pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component conditions.
Severe lattice distortion governs the proposed enhancement of plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr.
Improved grain-boundary cohesion governs the proposed enhancement of plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr.
The alloy has the equimolar composition W20Ta20Ti20V20Zr20.
Both WTaTiVZr and commercial tungsten will be tested in annealed, homogeneous initial microstructural states.
Commercial tungsten is an appropriate plasma-facing-material baseline.
Temperatures at or above 1000 °C are representative of high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr lowers the energy barrier for dislocation nucleation.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr lowers the energy barrier for dislocation mobility.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion in WTaTiVZr delays crack initiation.
Pure tungsten has higher barriers to dislocation movement than WTaTiVZr under the proposed conditions.
Higher barriers to dislocation movement cause pure tungsten to have limited plasticity and lower toughness during high-temperature deformation.
At comparable strain, WTaTiVZr will exhibit a higher dislocation density than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit more active dynamic recovery during high-temperature deformation than pure tungsten.
Crack nucleation will begin at a higher strain in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism may not apply below 1000 °C or at substantially different strain rates.

Identical high-temperature tensile tests with in-situ TEM can compare dislocation-density evolution, recovery behavior, crack-initiation strain, and stress–strain response between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
